correctness.rationale: PASS: The frozen result defines Haar-uniform unoriented great circles and the orthogonal spherical lune W={x>=0,y>=0}. With normal (a,b,c), endpoints at the two boundary meridians yield cos L=ab/sqrt((a^2+c^2)(b^2+c^2)); null exceptional normals excluded. |a| is uniform (0,1), azimuth of (b,c) uniform and independent. For 0<t<pi/2 conditional P(L<t||a|=u)=arctan(u tan t)/pi; integration gives F(t)=[t+cot(t)log(cos t)]/pi. Sign reflection extends to pi/2<t<pi with log|cos|; differentiation yields density -log|cos t|/(pi sin^2 t). Analytic symmetry, series in z=sin^2t, and midpoint expansion prove mean/median pi/2, strictly unimodal log cusp and central-band asymptotic. Independently integrated the conditional distribution at five t and checked reflection and derivative; density singularity is integrable, no mass. Geodesic intrinsic arc, not straight Euclidean chord or length-biased sampling.
